answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using remote hardware attestation. Agents must execute inside secure enclaves, emitting proofs anchored to umber silicon dies. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable capital cost of dedicated physical processors per identity, stopping an ocean of fake personas from dominating the execution horizon. However, enclaves depend on trusted chip manufacturers and remain vulnerable to microarchitectural side-channel leaks.
